forces: A ratified `ci-topology` requirement already states that CI workflows SHALL pin exact declared Node versions rather than floating major tags, so the sonar job's floating pin is a conformance violation and the repair may not restate or reinterpret that requirement.
`setup-node` resolves a floating major at run time, so the analyser's runtime can move with no commit and no diff; a gate that names specific majors cannot see a pin nobody enumerated.

`sonar` is one of ten required merge contexts, so when the analyser turns its recommended minimum into a hard one the job reds every pull request in the repository at once, with no code change to correlate against.

The sonar job installs SDK dependencies for type-aware analysis under an engine the package's `engines` range excludes, and with no `.npmrc` the mismatch warns instead of failing, so nothing stops the analysis running against that tree.

`compatibility.json` already declares `node.ciVersions` as the two supported releases, so the repair must move onto a declared release rather than introducing a third version the policy does not carry.

A floating-tag rule written against one literal major under-enforces the requirement it implements, so widening it must reject any bare major without failing closed on the six exact pins already in the workflow.

approach-add-22-to-the-existing-rule.reason: Repeats the defect it is meant to fix. The rule would then name two majors and stay silent about every other, and the failure mode is precisely a pin nobody enumerated: 22 entered the workflow as a carried-over value from another repository's workflow, not as a considered choice, so the next carried-over value would drift the same way.

approach-require-full-semver-everywhere.reason: Fails closed on legitimate future forms — a .nvmrc reference or a matrix expression — and converts a narrow anti-drift rule into a formatting mandate the ratified requirement does not make. The requirement forbids floating major tags; it does not prescribe one spelling for every other case.

evidence_ids: the sonar job requests 24.2.0, a release already listed in compatibility.json node.ciVersions, and its CI run emits neither the analyser's version-recommendation warning nor EBADENGINE for the SDK package
a planted floating "22" fails the widened coherence rule and passes the previous literal-26 rule, so the arm evidences the widening rather than restating a case already covered
all six exact pins in the workflow still pass, because the pattern requires the closing quote to follow the digits and so cannot match a dotted release

security_justification.trust_boundary: The analyser is a required merge gate, so the runtime it executes on is inside the trust boundary that decides whether code may land. A floating major lets that runtime change without a commit; pinning a declared release puts it back under review, and the widened rule keeps it there.
security_justification.authority_provenance: No actor, tenant, or authority value is read, derived, or emitted. The change alters which Node release a CI job requests and which shapes a coherence rule rejects; neither participates in event authority.
security_justification.authentication_or_authorization: No authentication or authorization decision changes. The sonar token and project key are untouched, and the quality gate continues to report on the same project key.
security_justification.audit_integrity: No audit event, catalog entry, or emitted record changes. The gate's own record — the coherence diagnostic — becomes more complete, since it now names any floating major rather than one literal.
security_justification.confidentiality: No data is read, stored, or transmitted that was not already. No credential, payload, or user data enters or leaves the changed paths.
security_justification.mutation_ownership: The workflow file is governance_core and is owned here by an explicit path inventory; the coherence rule and its controls are package-local governed paths already owned by this change. No path outside that inventory is written.
security_justification.fail_posture: Strictly fail-closed in both directions. The widened rule rejects a superset of what it rejected before and can admit nothing it previously refused, and the pinned job fails loudly on a version that does not exist rather than silently resolving a different one.
security_justification.error_disclosure: The renamed diagnostic reports only the rule name and the workflow path, with no file contents or caller data. Renaming it from the literal 26 prevents a misleading message that would name a major the rule no longer singles out.
security_justification.concurrency: No concurrency is introduced, removed, or reordered. The change adds no parallelism to CI and no asynchronous behaviour to the checker, which reads one file and applies one regular expression.
security_justification.lifecycle: No lifecycle state, transition, or ordering changes. The gate runs at the same point in the same chain, and no OpenSpec lifecycle rule is altered.
security_justification.resource_retention: Nothing is retained. The checker holds the workflow text for the duration of one synchronous read, and the change adds no cache, queue, or store.
security_justification.retry_or_redelivery: No retry or redelivery path changes. The sonar job's existing single scan retry is untouched, and this change neither adds nor removes an attempt.
security_justification.cryptography: No cryptographic material, algorithm, signature, or hash chain is introduced, read, or changed.
security_justification.privacy_transformation: No field transformation, redaction, or privacy policy is involved. No personal or tenant data is in scope.
security_justification.external_security_integration: SonarQube is an existing required gate and remains one; this change moves the runtime it executes on onto a supported release rather than integrating anything new. No SIEM, exporter, collector, or detection integration is added, which would require its own authorization.
